items: How to age wine at home?

Short Answer Keep bottles cool, dark, still and at a steady temperature, lying on their sides if they have corks, and choose wines that are actually built to age. The ideal conditions: Temperature: around 12–14°C. Consistency matters more than the exact number; frequent swings do more damage than a steady 16°C. Darkness: light, especially sunlight, can damage wine quickly. Humidity: around 60–70%

Why does Albariño taste so mineral and salty?

Short Answer There's no actual salt in the glass, but the sensation comes from a real combination of factors. Why does Albariño fly under the radar outside Spain?

What is alcohol content in wine?

Short Answer Most wine is between 11% and 15% alcohol by volume, and the number is printed on every label. Alcohol comes from sugar. Yeast eats the sugar in grape juice and produces alcohol, so riper grapes with more sugar make stronger wine. Why does Alsatian Riesling taste so fruity-aromatic?

Short Answer Alsace sits in the rain shadow of the Vosges mountains, which gives it a longer, drier, sunnier growing season than most of cool-climate France, and that extra hang time lets Riesling build up terpenes, the aromatic compounds responsible for its signature notes of lime blossom, white flowers, and stone fruit. Why does Alsatian Riesling taste so fruity and floral?

Alsace amplifies this: a continental climate sheltered by the Vosges mountains gives long, dry, sunny autumns, so grapes hang late and build aromatic intensity without losing acidity, since nights stay cool. Why is Argentinean Malbec so affordable?

Short Answer This is one of the rare cases where good wine and cheap wine aren't in tension. Land at altitude in Mendoza is genuinely inexpensive compared to Napa or Bordeaux, where proximity to famous villages inflates every hectare. Why is Arinto so mineral and crisp?

Short Answer Arinto is a late-ripening Portuguese grape with an unusual habit: it holds onto malic acid well past the point where most grapes have burned through theirs as sugar accumulates. That's not a cool-vintage fluke, it's just how the grape is wired, which is why Arinto stays crisp even in a hot year. Why is Australian Chardonnay sometimes generic?

Why does Australian Pinot Grigio taste so light and fruity?
